entry.title: ECCV 2026
entry.content:
At the CV4Ecology Workshop at ECCV 2026, Christoph presented two of our recent papers together with Hugo Markoff, showcasing new approaches to AI-based wildlife monitoring from aerial RGB and thermal video.

The first paper, When One Modality Is Not Enough: Multimodal Sex and Life-Stage Classification of Red Deer from Aerial RGB/Thermal Video, explores how combining RGB and thermal imagery can improve the classification of red deer by sex and life stage. By fusing complementary information from both sensors, the approach can handle cases where either modality alone is insufficient.

The second paper, Oh Deer, How Should I Handle This? Seasonal Priors for Selective Wildlife Annotation and Classification, investigates how seasonal biological changes can be incorporated into wildlife annotation and classification. The work shows how ecological knowledge and uncertainty-aware prediction can make automated monitoring more reliable.

Together, the two papers highlight the value of combining multimodal sensing, computer vision, and ecological knowledge for more robust and informative wildlife monitoring.

entry.title: SIGGRAPH 2026
entry.content:
This summer, Christoph Praschl represented our team at SIGGRAPH 2026 in Los Angeles, where he presented our latest work on synthetic data for wildlife detection.

The poster, “From Virtual Forests to Real Wildlife: Synthetic Non-Radiometric Thermal UAV Data for Animal Detection,” introduces a simulation pipeline that generates synthetic RGB and thermal drone imagery of forest environments, including automatically generated annotations for object detection, segmentation, and tracking.

A key focus of the work is the challenging sim-to-real transfer: training detection models on synthetic thermal data and evaluating them on real-world drone recordings of wildlife. The results show the potential of synthetic data to complement costly and difficult-to-acquire real-world datasets, particularly for applications in forest environments.

It was a great opportunity to share our research with the international computer graphics and computer vision community at SIGGRAPH Posters ’26, held July 19–23 in Los Angeles.

entry.title: CVPR2026
entry.content:
Our colleague Christoph Praschl attended this year’s CVPR 2026 in Denver. As part of the CV4Animals workshop, he presented the paper “The BAMBI Dataset: Multimodal Nadir UAV Recordings of Forest Wildlife” together with Hugo Markoff from Aalborg University (Denmark) and Sara Beery from MIT (USA).

The focus is on the drone-based wildlife dataset created as part of the BAMBI project. It comprises multimodal nadir recordings of wildlife in forest areas and forms an important foundation for AI-supported wildlife monitoring.

The presentation at the CV4Animals Workshop underscores the international relevance and collaborations of the BAMBI project and demonstrates how drone technology and computer vision are opening up new possibilities for nature conservation, wildlife ecology, and monitoring.

entry.title: MIE2026
entry.content:
Our colleagues Selina Adlberger and Natasha Trajkovska attended this year’s Medical Informatics Europe (MIE) conference in Genova, Italy, where they presented recent work from our research group.

Selina presented “Leveraging Synthetic Patient Data for Process Mining in Healthcare”, a contribution developed as part of our PICA project. The work explores how synthetic patient data can support process mining in healthcare while addressing challenges related to data availability, privacy, and reproducibility.

Natasha presented the pipeline “Process Mining on FHIR AuditEvents: Conformance Checking with a Standard Operating Procedure for Chest Pain”, implemented as part of the Treetop Medical project. Her presentation showed how FHIR AuditEvents can be used for process mining and conformance checking against a clinical standard operating procedure.

Together, both contributions highlight our group’s research on data-driven methods for analysing and improving healthcare processes.

Congratulations to Selina and Natasha on presenting their work at MIE 2026!

entry.title: dHealth 2026
entry.content:
Our research group was once again represented at this year’s dHealth Conference in Vienna by our colleague Andreas Pointner. There, he presented the paper “Managing Incompatible FHIR Implementation Guides in a Single Backend.” In his presentation, he used two examples from Germany to illustrate the challenges that can arise from incompatible FHIR implementation guides and how these can be elegantly resolved using namespaces in graph databases.

Since 2007, the dHealth Conference has been one of the most important events in the field of digital health and health informatics. Under the motto “Health Informatics meets Digital Health,” the conference brings together researchers, companies, public institutions, and healthcare organizations annually to discuss innovative digital solutions for a more efficient and higher-quality healthcare system. Of particular note is the close exchange between research and practice, which enables new perspectives and joint innovations.

entry.title: LREC 2026
entry.content:
Our colleague Sophie Bauernfeind attended this year’s Language Resources and Evaluation Conference (LREC), where she presented recent work at the CL4Health Workshop on Patient-Oriented Language Processing.

CL4Health brings together research on computational linguistics, healthcare, and patient-centered research. The workshop focuses on language technologies that improve access to trustworthy health information, support patient understanding, and enable explainable healthcare communication, including clinical data summarization, health question answering, text simplification, and patient-focused AI systems.

Sophie presented the paper “Patient-Specific Care Pathway Visualization for Medical Nursing Staff.” The work explores how patient-specific clinical information can be transformed into intuitive visual representations that support nursing staff in understanding individual care pathways. The paper investigates the use of generative AI for graph-based patient pathway visualization, assessing whether standard models can achieve explainable results without additional preprocessing or larger architectures.

(Photo by Andreas Stöckl)

entry.title: AIST Team Event 2026
entry.content:
This year’s annual AIST Team Event brought a refreshing change of pace. Instead of our traditional archery activity, we decided to hit the bowling lanes together for the first time. The event was a great opportunity to spend time as a team, share some fun moments, and celebrate our achievements together.

With this event, we also wanted to express our sincere appreciation to all our employees and current interns for their dedication, commitment, and excellent work throughout the year. And although some of the images might suggest otherwise, nobody was hurt during the event! 😀

Thank you all for being such an important part of the AIST team!

entry.title: International Visit
entry.content:
Over the past few weeks, we have been delighted to welcome some special international reinforcements to our research group. Several students and researchers from across Europe are currently actively contributing to our projects as part of internships, bringing valuable perspectives and fresh ideas to the table.

Ivan Ludoski from the University of Novi Sad in Serbia is supporting us. Also on site with us are Tamerlan Aslakhanov and Jasper Vandeput from PXL University (Belgium), who are intensively involved in our ongoing research as part of their internships.

Unfortunately, Hugo Markoff from Aalborg University (Denmark) was unable to travel here in person. Nevertheless, he is closely involved in the collaboration remotely and actively contributes to the international exchange.

We are very pleased about this collaboration and hope that these international connections will continue to grow in the future!

entry.title: GRIVAPP 2026
entry.content:
From March 9 to March 11, 2026, Christoph attended this year’s GRIVAPP Conference 2026 in Marbella, Spain. During the conference, he presented his current research titled “Evaluation of Novel View Synthesis in the Context of Radiometric Drone Imagery.”

In this work, he and his colleagues investigated how modern neural rendering approaches such as NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting perform on radiometric drone imagery. A particular highlight of the conference was the paper being honored with the Best Student Paper Award. The foundation for this work was laid as part of Sebastian Schoibesberger’s master’s thesis—congratulations on this outstanding achievement!

A heartfelt thank you goes to the conference organizers, especially Stefan Jänicke, Daniel Meneveaux, and the entire organizing team for the successful execution of the event.

entry.title: EUROCAST 2026
entry.content:
Mert, Natasha, Simone, Christoph, Oliver, and Gerald had the opportunity to be part of this year’s delegation of the University of Applied Sciences Upper Austria and to represent our research group at EUROCAST. At the International Conference on Computer Aided Systems Theory (EUROCAST 2026), several current research projects authored by our colleagues were presented. With contributions on trustworthy, explainable, and generative artificial intelligence, medical process analysis, ecological remote sensing, and industrial assistance systems, the papers reflected the thematic breadth of our research.

  • M. Dalkilic, C. Praschl – Guided Code Generation with Large Language Models and Static Code Analysis
  • C. Praschl, M.T. Karbasch, K. Probst, D.C. Schedl – Synthetic UAV Imagery for Ecological Monitoring Using Generative Artificial Intelligence
  • O. Krauss, A. Mileva – Explainable and Privacy-Preserving AI for Healthcare: A Local GraphRAG Pipeline for Nursing Care Guidelines
  • S. Sandler, O. Krauss – Combining Traditional Machine Learning and Generative AI to Create a Trustworthy Overview of Austrian Online Shops
  • N. Trajkovska, S. Kastenhofer, S. Sandler, S. Bauernfeind, C. Praschl, O. Krauss, R. Hecktor, D. Herzmanek, M. Roiss, M. Haider, M. Rechenmacher, D. Roth –Tracing Clinical Pathways from Unstructured Medical Documents: A Case Study on a Standard Operating Procedure for Chest Pain
  • G.A. Zwettler, M. Hanreich, K. Kloiber, J. Schönböck, J. Altmann – Human-Centered AI for Industrial Maintenance: Prototyping an LLM-Based Knowledge Platform

We would like to thank all participants for the inspiring scientific environment, the engaging discussions, and the valuable feedback on our presentations, as well as for the intensive professional exchange throughout the entire conference.
